transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-11-18 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Hale (Redwood SE), Jamal Price (Redwood SE), Aya Chen (Redwood CSM); Priya Rao (Atlas Head of ML), Tom Kline (Atlas DevOps), Sara Mitchell (Atlas Security), Diego Alvarez (SRE), Maya Li (Product).

Summary: Weekly pilot check-in for Redwood Private deployment in Atlas VPC. Walked through staging upgrade, remaining networking items, recent benchmark runs (odd p99 spikes), and security checklist. Action items captured at end.

00:00 Lena Ortiz: alright everyone, thanks for joining, um we only have 45 minutes so we'll go through updates from redwood, then tom and sara, then plan out load test next week
00:12 Priya Rao: thanks lena, quick note, we're on a tight timeline to stabilize this before the end of the month so anything we can do to reduce blockers helps
00:20 Marcus Hale: quick update from infra, we pushed the 1.4 runtime candidate into our staging pool yesterday, it includes improved kernel selection and a new batching heuristic — conversation earlier misread as kernel, but it's kernel selection logic and a memory patch for kv cache handling
00:38 Diego Alvarez: can you clarify kv cache? our last run showed an eviction pattern, and the transcript earlier said K V cash so just making sure the behavior is the same
00:45 Marcus Hale: yes kv cache like key-value, we found that long prefix reuse was causing high cache churn, the 1.4 patch improves cache pinning and reduces re-allocs 
00:58 Tom Kline: on our side we still have the peering tunnel flapping once every few hours, thought it might be NAT gateway timeouts but it seems route propagation on the peering link is intermittent
01:12 Jamal Price: ok we saw that in logs too, we think the issue is asymmetric routing when one of the TGWs has a more specific route, that triggers a small window of packet loss which spikes tail latency
01:30 Sara Mitchell: from security: we need cert rotation doc, KMS key policy and HSM integration details, plus audit log retention options — our compliance team needs those before we can sign off on private deployment
01:46 Lena Ortiz: noted, we'll attach the SOC2 package and a short doc on KMS/HSM integration. lena: i'll also add certificate rotation notes — our standard is 90 days but we can surface the rotation playbook
02:02 Priya Rao: performance: last week's benchmark results showed good throughput but odd p99 spikes around 6pm load window, did you correlate with the peering flaps?
02:18 Marcus Hale: partially — when the peering briefly routes across a fallback path requests hit a higher-hop path and latency jumps, plus the runtime fallback to smaller batch sizes increases token cost and adds jitter
02:33 Tom Kline: i can share the VPC flow logs and route tables, i'll also check TGW health checks, maybe the BGP session reset is the root cause
02:45 Marcus Hale: perfect please share the route tables; also we'd like you to enable flow logs in the staging account for the period of the next test so we can correlate packet loss to p99 spikes
02:58 Maya Li: quick product note — we're going to test with two workload shapes: chat (short, <256 tokens) and docs (longer, ~1024 tokens). we saw different batching behavior, chat needs lower latency, docs can accept more batching for cost reduction
03:15 Jamal Price: good call, our recommendation is batch-size 8 for docs, 1-2 for chat with aggressive prefix caching enabled, that'll keep tail latency lower for chat
03:30 Diego Alvarez: is there a config we should toggle in the runtime to prefer latency SLO over cost? we prioritized cost in staging and it manifested in those spikes
03:42 Marcus Hale: yes there's a routing policy flag and a batch target threshold — we can flip it to latency-first which will bias kernel selection and batching aggressiveness to keep p95 inside your SLO
03:58 Sara Mitchell: security follow-up — do you support customer-managed keys in HSM? the transcript earlier said K M S slash H S M and i think we need exact model support and rotation SOAP for our auditors
04:12 Jamal Price: we support CMK via AWS KMS and can integrate with HSM-backed keys; we'll provide the docs and the exact API call patterns for envelope encryption, plus example policy statements
04:30 Lena Ortiz: action items: lena: send SOW/pricing + security pack, marcus: run the 1.4 staging benchmark and share p95/p99, tom: share peering/route tables and flow logs, sara: send list of KMS/HSM questions
04:45 Priya Rao: one more onboarding question — what's the expected timeline for a production cutover if staging results look good? do we need a maintenance window for cert rotation or for traffic migration?
05:02 Marcus Hale: typical timeline is 2-3 weeks after green staging runs: one week to iron out networking, then a dry run traffic migration window (low traffic) followed by full cutover; cert rotation is separate and can be done rolling, shouldn't require large downtime
05:18 Tom Kline: for the dry run we'd want a canary route and A/B with our existing hosted provider, can you support split traffic policies?
05:28 Jamal Price: yes we support traffic routing by percent and region, canary early fallback policies are built-in; we also support automatic fallback to a hosted variant if private capacity is constrained
05:42 Maya Li: any blockers from our side about dedicated capacity? we may want to evaluate dedicated pools later for predictable throughput
05:50 Marcus Hale: dedicated is an option but for pilot we recommended VPC private deployment; once you hit sustained throughput a dedicated pool reduces jitter and gives SLA guarantees
06:05 Lena Ortiz: competitors were mentioned briefly: tom asked about Sagemaker and vertex for managed infra; we noted differences — cost and observability are primary differentiators for redwood
06:18 Priya Rao: ok, action items sound good. can you also share the benchmarking sheet you used, the one with batch sizes and seq lengths?
06:27 Marcus Hale: yes i'll share the benchmark spreadsheet link in slack and include the raw logs; note the 1.4 run had better median but still some 99th outliers that we want to triage with your flow logs
06:40 Diego Alvarez: one small note: our NAT gateway was in a shared account and there was a firewall rule change last week, that could explain the intermittent path change
06:52 Tom Kline: yep that change was rolled back but TBH we need better route propagation alerts — i'll add an alert to TGW health checks
07:05 Sara Mitchell: on the audit front — where are the API audit logs stored? are they pushed to our S3 in our account or kept in redwood logs? we prefer push to our account for longer retention
07:18 Jamal Price: we can push API audit logs to your S3 bucket via cross-account role; retention is configurable, default 90 days but we can extend based on compliance requirements
07:35 Lena Ortiz: ok recapping next steps: lena to send SOW+pricing+security pack (SOC2 docs, KMS/HSM integration, cert rotation playbook), marcus to run and share 1.4 benchmark and raw logs, tom to share route tables and flow logs and enable flow logs for next test, sara to compile KMS/HSM questions. plan load test week of 2027-11-22.
07:58 Priya Rao: cool, please cc compliance on the security pack and we'll follow up, thanks everyone
08:05 Lena Ortiz: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invite for the load test and ping slack with artifact links. meeting adjourned.

References/Shared artifacts: benchmarking-sheet (link), redwood-private-setup doc (link), SOC2 package (link), sample SOW (link).
